Trust Lens/Identity & Authorization

Platform Trust and Security Map

Public traffic crosses a trust boundary where authentication, token validation, policy checks, and secret access are enforced before private services handle the request.

Reading Notes

System Shape

  • Public clients enter through the API gateway, which sits at the edge of the trust boundary.
  • Inside the boundary, authentication, token validation, policy, and secrets are centralized before private services run.
  • The admin console is a privileged actor that crosses into the trust boundary for operations.

Critical Flows

  • Gateway forwards credentials to Auth Service; Auth validates tokens with the OIDC provider.
  • Policy Engine authorizes the request; Secrets Manager releases scoped credentials.
  • Only authenticated and authorized traffic reaches the Order Service and User DB.

Operational Notes

  • All control-plane calls are logged and auditable; privileged admin actions require break-glass approval.
  • Secrets are short-lived and scoped per request, never shared across tenants.
  • Token validation failure closes the request at the gateway before it touches private services.
Diagram type: trust map Scope: identity, authorization, and privileged access
